title: Finite-support sheaves and finite maps
statement:
A classical sheaf supported on finitely many closed points of a curve over an
algebraically closed field has no positive cohomology. Its sections are the
direct sum of its stalks, unchanged under algebraically closed extension. For
a finite morphism $h\colon Y\to C$, the direct image $h_*$ of classical
sheaves is exact, commutes with arbitrary base change, and satisfies
$H^q(C,h_*G)=H^q(Y,G)$.

steps.text:
Work first on the étale sites. Over a strict localization of $C$, a finite
scheme is a finite disjoint union of strictly henselian local schemes. Every
étale cover of such a local scheme has a section over its closed geometric
point, so global sections are exact there. This gives vanishing of the higher
direct images under $h$ and the usual stalk formula, which in turn gives
finite base change (Stacks, Tags 03QP, 0959; this is the calculation of
[sk-lem-pbc-finite]). A finite set of algebraically closed points has exact
sections, which gives the first assertion. Comparison of classical direct
images and [sk-prop-sf-comparison] transport these statements to the
pro-étale site.
